title: Conditional Optimal Bridge for Riemannian Activation Steering
claim: Residual-stream norms stay nearly constant across layers, so activations effectively lie on a hypersphere and direction matters more than magnitude.
layout: 4 panels in a row, shared axes, one line-and-band plot per model
description: Four side-by-side line plots, one for each LLM: Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Falcon-7B and Mistral-7B. The x-axis is layer index (0 to about 30, or 0 to 27 for Qwen). The y-axis is normalized residual norm, from 0.6 to 1.4. Each panel has a flat horizontal line at 1.0 with a translucent shaded band for the 25th–75th percentile. The bands are very narrow. Each model has its own color: blue, pink or purple, teal and green. A small boxed label in the lower right gives the coefficient of variation: 7.1%, 2.5%, 6.7% and 7.3%. The eye goes to the flat lines and thin bands, which show that the norm is nearly constant across layers and models. The plots are minimal, with no legend.
caption: Last-token residual-stream norms across layers on TruthfulQA for four LLMs, each divided by its layer-wise mean. Dark and light bands show the 25th--75th percentiles. The coefficient of variation (CoV) is reported per model.
abstract: Activation steering offers a lightweight alternative to fine-tuning for controlling large language models at inference time. Many existing steering methods implicitly optimize a log-density-ratio objective between desired and undesired activation distributions without a principled derivation. Methods with fixed steering directions can also degrade out-of-distribution (OOD) performance. We introduce Conditional Optimal Bridge for Riemannian Activation Steering (\textsc{Cobras}), which casts steering as a SchrÃ¶dinger Bridge on the residual-stream hypersphere. This formulation yields a principled derivation of the log-density-ratio steering objective from a well-posed optimization problem. We construct a query-adaptive steering field that recovers log-density-ratio steering as a limiting case. The fitted transport also provides a support score for controlling OOD interventions. Across four models, \textsc{Cobras} outperforms prior steering methods in nearly all model--task settings spanning helpfulness, truthfulness, and detoxification, while largely preserving OOD performance. The code is available \href{https://github.com/arshandalili/cobras}{here}.
